correctness.rationale: For every fixed \(p\equiv1\pmod3\) and B, \(f(X)=X^2+X+1\) has simple unit roots modulo p and therefore roots modulo \(p^B\). The set of primes q in each lifted reduced class has divergent reciprocal sum. Exact finite CRT probabilities for \(q\parallel m\) tend to a zero avoidance product; \(\sigma(m^2)\) is divisible by \(p^B\) on density one. For finite P of primes \(p>T\), this \(p^2\) divisibility makes \(p\parallel m\) imply \(p\mid R(m)\). The CRT upper density of simultaneously avoiding \(p\parallel m\) is product(\(1-1/p+1/p^2\)), tending to zero as P grows; no unproven infinite independence is used. The prime-power gcd valuations and all limits were reconstructed; exact finite verifier matches cited numerical counts and congruence identities. Infinite theorem relies on the proved reduction plus Dirichlet reciprocal-prime divergence, not on a finite census.

originality.rationale: The exact zero-density assertion appears as Conjecture 5.1 in Dris [2022], following a weaker theorem. Meyerowitz [2020] supplies the central root heuristic but conditions the Euler product on unproved justification; the present finite-CRT sieve closes that gap and proves stronger ratio divergence. Relevant published gcd and sum-of-divisors literature, indexed records, and OEIS entries do not imply this statement. Unindexed equivalent work remains a risk.
